questions.question: What is the primary focus of the philosophy of language?

options.A: The grammatical rules governing written communication
options.B: The nature of human language, its origins and use, the relationship between meaning and truth, and how language relates to human thought and reality
options.C: The historical development of spoken dialects across cultures
options.D: The biological mechanisms behind human speech production

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that philosophy of language investigates the nature of human language, its origins and use, the relationship between meaning and truth, and how language relates to human thought and understanding, as well as to reality itself.

questions.question: According to the text, what have philosophers long been concerned with regarding language?

options.A: The aesthetic qualities of poetic language
options.B: The speed at which language evolves over generations
options.C: The systematic way in which language carries information about the world
options.D: The differences between spoken and written language

questions.explanation: The opening sentence states that philosophers have long been concerned with the systematic way in which language carries information about the world.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a central question in the philosophy of language?

options.A: Why do some languages have more words than others?
options.B: What it means for a word to make reference and how meaning corresponds to reality
options.C: How children acquire language faster than adults
options.D: Whether written language is superior to spoken language

questions.explanation: The text identifies as a central question what it means for a word to make reference — what it is for language to mean something, and how that meaning corresponds to reality.

questions.question: What is the question about thought and language posed in the text?

options.A: Whether language shapes culture more than culture shapes language
options.B: Whether a form of language is necessary for thought — do people think in language, or think and then translate thoughts into language
options.C: Whether animals can develop language-based thought
options.D: Whether mathematical language is a form of natural language

questions.explanation: The text presents the question of whether a form of language is necessary for thought — specifically whether people think in language, or whether they think and then translate those thoughts into language.

questions.question: According to Baykent (2016), how is the philosophy of language defined as a field?

options.A: A branch of cognitive science studying how the brain processes words
options.B: The field where philosophical questions about language are discussed and where language, language ability, and the language we speak are viewed philosophically
options.C: A discipline focused exclusively on the logical structure of sentences
options.D: The study of how language policies are formed in governments

questions.question: According to the text (citing Kutas, 2013), how many central problems has the philosophy of language been concerned with?

options.A: Two
options.B: Three
options.C: Four
options.D: Five

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the four central problems of the philosophy of language?

options.A: The nature of meaning
options.B: Language use
options.C: Language translation
options.D: Language cognition

questions.question: What is the fourth central problem of the philosophy of language mentioned in the text?

options.A: The origin of language
options.B: The relationship between language and reality
options.C: The diversity of human languages
options.D: The development of writing systems

questions.explanation: The text lists the four central problems as: the nature of meaning, language use, language cognition, and the relationship between language and reality.
